group_assessment.weighting: Two halves. The clinical-pathology half (Valencia pathology and urology, FIVO) supplies the cohort, grading and scoring: descriptive_clinical, and competent at histological grading, weighed as observation. The WWOX half (Aldaz laboratory, a founding WWOX group) supplies the antibody, whose validation is imported from that group's earlier papers rather than shown here. Neither group works on WWOX-related neurological disease. The prognostic conclusions are the authors' interpretation of bivariate associations and are weighed below the observations.

entries.proposition: COHORT: 101 patients, NONCONSECUTIVE primary bladder tumours, 81 TUR and 20 cystectomy specimens. DATO. How the 101 were selected from a non-consecutive series is not stated (searched Methods), so selection bias cannot be assessed.
entries.snippet: The study group encompassed 101 patients with nonconsecutive primary bladder tumours [81 transurethral resection (TUR) and 20 radical cystectomy specimens].
entries.anchor: Materials and methods > Clinicopathological data, sentence 1

experimental_context.system: human primary bladder tumour tissue, retrospective single-series IHC

entries.proposition: GRADING/STAGING by two independent uropathologists with consensus. DATO.
entries.snippet: Subsequently, assessment of grade and stage was carried out by two independent uropathologists and consensus was reached in cases of discrepancy.
entries.anchor: Materials and methods > Clinicopathological data, paragraph 1

entries.proposition: CONTROLS: normal urothelium and squamous metaplasia from non-cancer patients. DATO.
entries.snippet: Likewise, normal bladder urothelium and squamous metaplasia were obtained from a control group of non-cancer patients.
entries.anchor: Materials and methods > Clinicopathological data, paragraph 2

entries.proposition: REAGENT AMBIGUITY: primary antibody given as '140 mg / ml' at 1:400. DATO as printed; the unit is implausible for a polyclonal stock and may be a conversion of a micro sign, but the version of record is not available here, so it is recorded as unresolved, not corrected.
entries.snippet: Primary polyclonal antibody was a rabbit anti-WWOX (140 mg / ml) with an optimal dilution of 1:400.

entries.proposition: IMPORTED VALIDATION: antibody specificity is asserted by citation (refs 7, 9, 10), not shown in this paper - no blocking peptide, knockdown tissue or western in this work. DATO about the citation; the specificity itself is a premise here.
entries.snippet: Specificity and sensitivity of the WWOX antibody employed and raised against the WW domains of this protein have been previously demonstrated in various publications.

entries.proposition: SCORING: subjective, two uropathologists, combined score. DATO. No inter-observer agreement statistic and no statement of blinding to outcome appear anywhere (searched kappa, interobserver, blind: zero hits).
entries.snippet: The immunoreaction was subjectively evaluated by two experienced uropathologists by using a combined score system.

entries.proposition: NEGATIVE CONTROL: primary antibody omission only. DATO.
entries.snippet: Lack of primary antibody was used as the negative control of the reaction.

entries.proposition: SCORE: intensity (0-3) multiplied by percentage category (0-4), range 0-12. DATO.
entries.snippet: a combined score was obtained by multiplying the intensity of the reaction and the percentage of stained tumour cells, which resulted in a final value ranging between 0 and 12 arbitrary units

entries.proposition: CATEGORIES: 0-4 low, 5-7 moderate, >7 high. DATO. COMPUTED: the products of 0-3 by 0-4 can only be 0,1,2,3,4,6,8,9,12, so 'moderate 5-7' contains the single value 6 and 'high' is 8, 9 or 12. The three categories are therefore unequal and 'moderate' is one score value.
entries.snippet: To simplify these data, scores ranging from 0 to 4 were considered a low level of WWOX protein expression, between 5 and 7 was considered moderate, and >7 was considered high.
entries.anchor: Materials and methods > Immunohistochemistry, paragraph 2, last sentence

entries.proposition: STATISTICS NAMED 'MULTIVARIATE' ARE PCA: the multivariate analysis is a principal component analysis for visualisation, not a multivariable regression. DATO. No Cox model or any adjusted analysis exists in the paper (searched Cox: zero hits).
entries.snippet: Multivariate analysis was performed by principal component analysis in order to simplify the dataset into a lower dimension analysis in three axes.

entries.proposition: THE P-VALUES OF THE ASSOCIATIONS are Kendall tau-b correlation tests between pairs of coded variables. DATO. They are bivariate and unadjusted; no multiplicity correction is mentioned.
entries.snippet: Variables were codified and then compared by means of Kendall’s τ-b correlation coefficient.

entries.proposition: SCORE DISTRIBUTION IN THE TEXT: low 26 (25.7%), moderate 25 (24.8%), high 50 (49.5%). DATO. These match the column sums of the grade rows of Table 2 (26, 25, 50), computed.
entries.snippet: low level (26 cases, 25.7%), moderate (25 cases, 24.8%) and high (50 cases, 49.5%)

entries.proposition: INTERNAL CONTRADICTION IN TABLE 2: the Total row prints 18 (17.8%) low, 33 (32.7%) moderate, 50 (45.5%) high. It disagrees with the text (26/25/50) and with the sums of every block of its own table (grade rows sum to 26/25/50; 50/101 is 49.5%, not 45.5%). DATO for both printings; the Total row is the one out of line with the table's own data.
AGE IN TEXT: mean 68.1, range 42-91; male 85.1%. DATO.
entries.snippet: The mean patient age was 68.1 years (range 42–91 years); 86 were male (85.1%) and 15 female (14.9%)

entries.proposition: AGE IN TABLE 1: range 38-91, and male 85.2% - a second minor text/table discrepancy (age floor 42 vs 38). DATO for both.
entries.snippet: Mean patient age 68.1 years (range 38–91)

entries.proposition: TOTAL ABSENCE of WWOX staining in 4 cases (4%), all urothelial carcinomas with extensive squamous metaplasia. DATO.
entries.snippet: In addition, a total absence of WWOX protein expression could be observed in four cases (4%), all of which were urothelial carcinomas with extensive squamous metaplasia

experimental_context.system: human primary bladder tumour tissue, retrospective single-series IHC

entries.proposition: FIG 3 LEGEND: squamous-metaplasia carcinomas displayed complete absence of WWOX. DATO as the legend.
entries.snippet: Urothelial carcinomas with extensive squamous metaplasia displayed a complete absence of WWOX protein expression.

entries.proposition: FIGURE 3, NATIVE PIXELS. A: H&E of a squamous carcinoma area. B: WWOX IHC high power, tumour cells essentially unstained - agrees with the legend - but a small group of cells at the upper-right margin carries a light brown cytoplasmic tint, whose identity (tumour or not) cannot be determined from the panel. 'Complete absence' holds for the field's tumour cells as far as can be judged; one field, one case, no internal positive control visible.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Figure 3: A haematoxylin and eosin squamous tumour field; B WWOX immunostain with blue nuclei and unstained cytoplasm across the field except a small brown-tinted cell group at the upper right edge.
entries.qualifies_needle: displayed a complete absence of WWOX protein expression

entries.proposition: UNTESTED PAIRWISE CLAIM: pTa 28/47 (59.6%) high vs pT1 11/23 (47.8%), called 'significantly lower (P = 0.002)'. DATO as printed. The 0.002 is the printed P of the Stage row of Table 2 (the three-level stage association), not a pTa-versus-pT1 test; no pairwise test is described.
entries.snippet: higher levels of WWOX protein immunoreactivity were observed in 28 out of 47 (59.6%) non-invasive neoplasms (pTa tumours) when compared with 11 out of 23 (47.8%) pT1 carcinomas in which the level of WWOX reactivity was significantly lower (P = 0.002).

entries.proposition: OUTCOME EVENTS over mean 42.2 months: 33 recurrences, 25 progressions, 19 disease deaths. DATO.
entries.snippet: during this period 33 patients (32.7%) presented recurrent disease, 25 (24.8%) showed tumour progression in grade and / or stage and 19 (18.8%) died of their disease.

entries.proposition: ASSOCIATIONS REPORTED: WWOX inversely correlated with grade (P = 0.001), stage (0.002), size (0.040) and progression (0.028). DATO for the P-values; the effect sizes are only in Figure 4B.
entries.snippet: in the case of WWOX protein expression an inverse correlation with histological grade (P = 0.001), tumour stage (P = 0.002), tumour size (P = 0.040) and tumour progression (P = 0.028) could be observed

experimental_context.system: human primary bladder tumour tissue, retrospective single-series IHC

entries.proposition: AUTHORS' STRENGTH WORD: 'strongly associated' with grade. DATO as their wording.
entries.snippet: Importantly, loss of WWOX protein expression was strongly associated in our series with tumour grade.

entries.proposition: FIGURE 4B, NATIVE PIXELS - THE EFFECT SIZES THE TEXT OMITS. Kendall tau-b of WWOX with: grade -0.319, stage -0.277, size (T) -0.175, N+ -0.150, M+ -0.031, multiplicity -0.123, progression -0.191, recurrence -0.021; P-values above the diagonal match the text. The largest correlation is about -0.32, a weak-to-moderate association in a bivariate unadjusted test, and progression is -0.19. 'Strongly associated' describes the P-value, not the size. Figure 4A is a three-factor loading plot with WWOX loading alone on negative factor 2. Label typo 'Kendal's'.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Figure 4B: correlation matrix, lower triangle Kendall tau-b, WWOX column -0.319 Grade, -0.277 Stage, -0.175 T, -0.150 N+, -0.031 M+, -0.123 Multiplicity, -0.191 Progression, -0.021 Recurrence; upper triangle P-values.
entries.qualifies_needle: strongly associated in our series with tumour grade

experimental_context.system: human primary bladder tumour tissue, retrospective single-series IHC

entries.proposition: UNIVARIATE CONTRASTS: PUNLMP vs HGUC P = 0.012; squamous-metaplasia carcinomas vs all pure urothelial P = 0.001. DATO. The squamous group is n = 5 (Table 2).
entries.snippet: the level of WWOX protein expression was significantly different between PUNLMP and HGUC (P = 0.012), and especially between UCSC and all the remaining pure urothelial tumours (P = 0.001)

entries.proposition: TEXT: non-invasive vs muscle-invading, P = 0.003 (Figure 5A,B). DATO as printed.
entries.snippet: As regards tumour stage, significant differences between non-invasive tumours and muscle-invading carcinomas were also observed (P = 0.003)

entries.proposition: TEXT: lowest vs high WWOX differ in progression, P = 0.029 (Figure 5C). DATO as printed.
entries.snippet: significant differences in terms of tumour progression were also observed between those cases showing the lowest levels of WWOX protein expression and those with high levels of WWOX immunoexpression (P = 0.029)

entries.proposition: FIG 5 LEGEND: panels are grade (A), stage (B) and TUMOUR SIZE (C). DATO as the legend.
entries.snippet: anova graphs show the statistical correlation of grade (A) stage (B) and tumour size (C) with respect to WWOX expression levels in univariate studies.

entries.proposition: FIGURE 5C, NATIVE PIXELS - THE LEGEND IS WRONG. Panel C plots WWOX expression (mean +/- 2SE) for Progression No vs Yes, P = 0.029 - it is the progression comparison the running text cites, not tumour size as the legend says. No tumour-size panel exists in Figure 5.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Figure 5C: x axis labelled Progression with categories No and Yes, y axis WWOX expression (mean plus or minus 2SE), P = 0.029 printed.

experimental_context.system: human primary bladder tumour tissue, retrospective single-series IHC

entries.proposition: FIGURE 5A-B, NATIVE PIXELS. B is labelled Stage I, II, III (not the pTa/pT1/pT2-4 of the text and tables) and prints P = 0.004, while the text cites P = 0.003 for the stage difference. A (grade, four groups) prints P < 0.0001, a figure given nowhere in the text; its UCSM interval runs below 0 (about -1 to 3.7) on a 0-12 score, i.e. a parametric mean +/- 2SE on n = 5 ordinal values. ANOVA on an ordinal product score is the test used.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Figure 5A-B: A grade categories PUNLMP, LGPUC, HGUC, UCSM with P < 0.0001 and the UCSM interval extending below zero; B stage categories I, II, III with P = 0.004.

experimental_context.system: human primary bladder tumour tissue, retrospective single-series IHC

entries.proposition: NULLS: no correlation with multiplicity (P = 0.11) or metastatic disease (N 0.067, M 0.379). DATO. The text prints 'N orMstatus'.
entries.snippet: In contrast, WWOX protein levels did not correlate with tumour multiplicity (P = 0.11) or metastatic disease

entries.proposition: COUNTER-DIRECTIONAL CELL: among the 7 M+ patients, 4 (57.1%) are WWOX-high and 0 moderate - the opposite direction to the grade/stage trend, on n = 7, P = 0.379. DATO.
KM PFS: loss of WWOX associated with shorter progression-free survival (Figure 6A). DATO; the text gives no P here (the abstract gives 0.042).
entries.snippet: Kaplan–Meier estimates corroborated a significant correlation between the loss of WWOX protein immunoreactivity and a shorter PFS

entries.proposition: NULL: no association with recurrence-free survival (and OS, per this sentence). DATO.
entries.snippet: However, no statistical association could be demonstrated regarding recurrence-free survival and OS

entries.proposition: OS: borderline, P = 0.053. DATO. Not significant at the paper's own 0.05 threshold.
entries.snippet: Moreover, loss of WWOX protein immunoexpression was of borderline significance for the prediction of OS (P = 0.053)

entries.proposition: AUTHORS' CONCLUSION: 'progressive loss' predicts progressive disease. DATO as wording; INFERENZA of the authors.
entries.snippet: Furthermore, progressive loss of WWOX protein expression appears to be useful in predicting progressive disease in urothelial bladder carcinoma.

entries.proposition: FIGURE 6, NATIVE CROPS - THE CURVES ARE NOT A GRADIENT. Three strata (negative/weak red, moderate green, strong blue), log-rank over three groups. A progression: P = 0.0421; red falls to ~0.55, but GREEN (moderate) ends ~0.84, ABOVE BLUE (strong) ~0.77. B recurrence: P = 0.54. C overall survival: P = 0.053; green ~0.84, blue ~0.81, red ~0.53. The contrast is low versus the rest, not a dose-response across levels, so 'progressive loss' is not what the strata show. Y axes are truncated (A and C start at 0.5, B at 0.4), which enlarges the visual separation. Censoring ticks shown; no numbers at risk; no adjusted model.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Figure 6: three Kaplan-Meier panels, A Progression P = 0.0421 with the red curve lowest and green above blue, B Recurrence P = 0.54, C Overall survival P = 0.053 with green above blue above red; y axes starting at 0.5, 0.4 and 0.5.
entries.anchor: Figure 6A-C (PDF p.14), two native crops of the 896x2080 raster
entries.qualifies_needle: progressive loss of WWOX protein expression appears to be useful

experimental_context.system: human primary bladder tumour tissue, retrospective single-series IHC

entries.proposition: AUTHORS' OWN CAVEAT: WWOX loss may be consequential to other alterations rather than causal. DATO as their limitation - it is the sentence that bounds everything above to association.
entries.snippet: The possibility exists, however, that alterations affecting the WWOX gene and protein expression are consequential to other genetic alterations rather than being a primary causative factor in bladder carcinogenesis.

entries.proposition: AUTHORS' LIMITATION: too few squamous-metaplasia carcinomas for robust statistics. DATO.
entries.snippet: Unfortunately, the number of urothelial carcinomas with extensive squamous metaplasia was not high enough for a more robust statistical analysis.

entries.proposition: LOCALISATION SPECULATION: perinuclear enhancement 'probably' Golgi. IPOTESI of the authors - no Golgi marker or co-staining in the paper.
entries.snippet: immunohistochemistry of WWOX protein in our study displayed intense granular cytoplasmic reactivity with a perinuclear enhancement of the reaction probably localized to the Golgi apparatus

entries.proposition: NORMAL TISSUE: strong diffuse staining in 10 normal urothelia and 5 squamous metaplasias without tumour. DATO.
entries.snippet: Strong and diffuse WWOX immunoreactivity was observed in 10 patients with normal bladder urothelium as well as in five with squamous metaplasia, all of them without tumour.

entries.proposition: PATTERN: granular cytoplasmic, no nuclear reactivity, in normal urothelium and metaplasia. DATO.
entries.snippet: In both normal urothelium and squamous metaplasia, WWOX immunoexpression consistently showed strong and diffusely granular cytoplasmic immunoreactivity without any nuclear reactivity.

entries.proposition: FIGURES 1-2, NATIVE PIXELS. Fig 1: normal urothelium intensely brown across the full urothelial thickness, stroma weak. Fig 2: A-B low-grade papillary tumour intense granular cytoplasmic staining, nuclei unstained; C-D high-grade invasive carcinoma weak, pale staining. Single representative fields; they illustrate the categories and quantify nothing.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Figures 1 and 2: normal urothelium strong brown cytoplasmic immunostain; low-grade papillary tumour intense granular cytoplasmic stain in 2A and 2B; high-grade carcinoma weak pale stain in 2C and 2D; nuclei blue.
entries.anchor: Figures 1 and 2 (PDF p.9-10), native rasters 1526x606 and 1552x1233

experimental_context.system: human primary bladder tumour tissue, retrospective single-series IHC

entries.proposition: TREATMENT CONFOUND: 11 of 20 cystectomy patients (55%) are WWOX-low versus 7/39 TUR-alone and 8/42 TUR-plus-adjuvant (P = 0.024). DATO. Treatment differs by WWOX level and the survival analyses are unadjusted, so treatment and stage are not separated from WWOX in Figure 6.
CITATION ERROR: an ovarian-cancer RFS result is attributed to ref 11, which is Qin 2006 on PROSTATE cancer; the ovarian WWOX paper is ref 10. DATO from the reference list.
entries.snippet: In ovarian tumours, loss of WWOX protein expression correlated with histological tumour type and tumour stage; and presented, furthermore, a strong statistical correlation with shorter RFS of patients.

entries.proposition: REFERENCE 11 IS A PROSTATE PAPER (the object of the citation error above). DATO; this locator quotes back matter deliberately.
entries.snippet: 11.Qin HR, Iliopoulos D, Semba S, et al. A role for the WWOX gene in prostate cancer.

entries.proposition: DEPENDENCY RELATION: ref 20 (Expression of Concern) is cited as background for WWOX restoration in lung cancer cells. DATO; citation only.
entries.snippet: Similar findings have been recently described by Qin et al. in prostate cells and tissues and by Fabbri et al. in lung cancer cell lines.
